class: Any test whose expected value was produced by running the code under test (instead of taken from the spec or an independent computation) passes whatever the code does, so a defect in the code is locked in as the 'correct' answer and the suite stays green.
mechanism: Builders wrote the implementation first, then asserted the values it returned; independent verifiers who recomputed the values from the spec found the mismatch.

first_seen.where: W-004 tests/table/test_table.py (leg Greek cells per-unit unsigned while TOTAL is position-level; test asserted -0.4125 for a sold put whose position delta is about +30.9) and W-016 tests/strategy/test_builder_history.py (asserted history_entries()[-1].legs == CONDOR_LEGS, i.e. the pre-change snapshot under the change's label)
first_seen.evidence: W-004 verifier: sum of leg delta cells -0.3746 vs TOTAL 4.5750, test green (12 passed). W-016 verifier: restore('User modified strike') returned 22800 after a change to 22750, test green (22 passed).

occurrences.evidence: position Greeks built from 4-dp-rounded per-unit values x quantity (gamma ~10% wrong: 0.0300 vs 0.0335); the test pinned POSITION_GREEKS[3].gamma == 0.0300, taken from the code's output
test set the snapshot's data_health=quote.health by hand, hiding that the record-level health is caller-supplied; with a stale deciding input the record said AVAILABLE

fix: Builder brief rule (every future brief): expected values come from the spec or an independent hand computation, never from the code's own output; add consistency tests (leg rows sum to totals; restore-by-label returns the labelled state). Independent verifiers recompute expected values from the spec (already their brief).

detection.note: Third occurrence (W-004 twice, W-016 once). Mechanism strengthened: builder brief rule + tests must compute expected numeric values with an independent implementation written in the test (e.g. Black-Scholes via math.erf, importing nothing from the code under test); verifiers recompute independently. Still no automated detector of where an expected value came from; a candidate check: an AST test flagging numeric literals with >=4 decimals in tests of computed Greeks without an independent helper — not built.
